reason: E1 explicitly states that coherent ordered nanoprecipitates can enhance strength without sacrificing coercivity, but it does not demonstrate an increase in coercivity—it aims to avoid sacrificing it. E2 shows that precipitates act as pinning centers and their dissolution softens the alloy magnetically, supporting the pinning premise, but neither passage provides evidence that Al additions or aging at 700°C produce the claimed coercivity increase in FeCoNi. The key premises about Al-induced precipitation and the specific heat treatment are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates can pin magnetic domain walls and increase coercivity
Adding Al to FeCoNi-based HEAs can form ordered nanoprecipitates
Aging at ~700°C will produce nanoscale coherent precipitates in Al-added FeCoNi
Domain wall pinning by precipitates boosts coercivity without major loss of saturation magnetization
The baseline FeCoNi HEA has coercivity ≤100 Oe
